title: Promoting a healthy culture within engineering teams
description: Academic case study of engineering culture after an acquisition, based on an anonymized AI-services company. It proposes a change approach using SWOT, empathy maps, RASCI, and ADKAR.
abstract: Academic case study from 2023 on how to rebuild a healthier engineering culture after an acquisition. The case uses an anonymized B2B2C company that sells AI services and grew very quickly and reached more than 600 people in several countries. Leadership changes and departmental restructuring were followed by favoritism in promotions, technical decisions concentrated in a few people, little support for career development, less psychological safety, and people leaving. The study proposes a practical way to rebuild that culture. It looks at the maturity of technical leadership, how teams work together, and whether the environment is safe enough to learn. The suggested approach reads the situation with SWOT, empathy maps, RASCI, and system diagrams, then works on shared agreements, clearer career paths, and training in leadership and collaboration. The change itself is framed with the ADKAR model.

title: Adventure Works Cycles, a business intelligence project
description: Academic BI project on the Adventure Works Cycles sample data. I built an ETL pipeline, a star-schema warehouse, and dashboards in Power BI and Qlik Sense.
abstract: Academic business-intelligence project from 2018, built on the Adventure Works Cycles sample data, the fictional manufacturing and distribution company used in BI courses. The exercise looks at the distance between a complex transactional database and the questions a management team would ask when demand changes. I analyzed the sources, extracted and consolidated the data, and modeled a star schema around sales facts, with dimensions for customers, sales territories, and products. The result is a set of dashboards in Power BI and Qlik Sense for regional sales, customer segments, and descriptive forecasts. It is a course project on sample data, not a system delivered to a real company.

title: Circuitos, discover your artistic hub
description: UX concept for a mobile product to find cultural events and city routes. I contributed to the research, the product concept, and the interface prototypes. Course work, 2017.
abstract: UX course concept from 2017 for a mobile product that helps people find cultural events and places in the city, such as design centers, local museums, and street art, when those schedules and spots are scattered. The concept has three parts. A local event list with personal scheduling, geolocated routes through curated cultural paths, and local storage for personal notes and favorites. I contributed to the research, the product concept, and the interface prototypes. It is a design concept from the course, not a shipped application.

title: Agent Orchestrator, a real-time AI telemetry dashboard
description: Dashboard of status and telemetry for simulated AI agents, built with Vue 3, TypeScript, and Docker.

title: An idea for an application to promote cultural activities
description: Master's project on a business case for a product to promote cultural events in Barcelona, including market analysis, a business model, and a marketing plan.
type: e-Business Concept and Market Niche Analysis
abstract: Master's project from 2020, a business case for a digital product that would promote artistic and cultural events in Barcelona. It starts from the gap between general local listings and audiences looking for very specific kinds of culture. The case includes a market-entry analysis, with target audiences and competitors, a monetization model, and an online marketing plan with acquisition channels and operating indicators. Delivery is sketched as an agile timeline and a software stack kept inside a budget. It is a planning document for a concept, not a company that was launched.

title: TMDB catalog for movies and series
description: Full-stack web application designed for anyone who loves movies and TV shows. It provides a seamless, fast way to browse a comprehensive catalog of titles, giving you all the details you need in one place. You can explore a wide variety of content through a user-friendly interface.

title: Pokédex, gotta catch 'em all
description: Progressive web application (PWA) built under Svelte, a modern JavaScript framework. It leverages the Pokémon API to provide a comprehensive and engaging Pokédex experience, data persistence with LocalStorage, the SpeechSynthesis, and Plotly charts.

title: Restaurant finder
description: Progressive web app to find nearby restaurants with the Geolocation API. It does not take orders or handle delivery.

title: Visualization Dashboard for Monitoring
description: Web application designed to help you easily understand complex data. Using the powerful D3.js library, it creates interactive and visually engaging charts for a business intelligence dashboard. You can effortlessly switch between different timeframes—by day, week, month, or year—to analyze error reports and other data.

title: Management Dashboard
description: Management dashboard designed to streamline employee data handling. It's a simple web application that provides you with complete control over your team's information. With straightforward CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) functionality.

title: Express API Backend Architecture
description: REST API boilerplate with Node.js, Express, MongoDB, Docker, Jest, and Supertest. A reference structure for a small API, not a system in production.

title: Basic Sticky Notes
description: A clean, interactive digital board application for managing virtual sticky notes. Features smooth drag-and-drop interactions, resizing, auto-save editing, and full keyboard navigation with client-side persistence.

title: Management System Pricing Calendar simulation with React, TypeScript, and TanStack Query
description: An interactive revenue-management simulation with dynamic rate visualization. Built on a decoupled full-stack architecture, with an API server and reactive data flows.

title: Basic Sticky Notes board with React, TypeScript, and Vite
description: An interactive sticky notes board built on a warm paper surface with real pad colors. Features custom dragging, pointer-driven resizing, context grouping, automatic localStorage persistence, and robust accessibility standards.

title: Semantic Graph CLI
description: Standalone TypeScript CLI plugin for Engram that reads memory data through a local HTTP server to generate deterministic semantic graph snapshots in JSON. Handles project-scoped filtering, stale lifecycle observation checks, and atomic file publication without mutating core data.

title: Type-safe GraphQL API (Domain-driven)
description: GraphQL API in progress with TypeScript and Apollo Server. It includes end-to-end types, custom scalars, data loading, generated docs, and an experimental natural-language query layer. Not released.

title: Cognitive Usability Analysis Tool
description: Experimental command-line tool inspired by cognitive usability principles. Analyzes web interfaces from a human-centered perspective to help identify friction points and improve clarity. Currently in early development.

title: Team-Memory-Health (TMH)
description: Agent-native CLI and skill to evaluate the qualitative pulse and alignment of a development team's shared memory. Analyzes coherence, freshness, coverage, and source distribution without assigning individual scores or mutating data.
